name: Volite / Volift

card.summary: Juvéderm Volite is a low-concentration hyaluronic acid gel injected into the skin for smoothness and hydration; trial data exist but are mostly single-arm and manufacturer-linked.
card.note: Volift is a separate product name; the skin-quality gel is Volite. Evidence is mostly single-arm or manufacturer-linked.

quick.overview:
Juvéderm Volite (also marketed as Skinvive, with the gel called VYC-12) is a crosslinked hyaluronic acid gel placed in the skin rather than beneath it, aiming to improve smoothness, hydration and fine texture rather than add volume. Volift is a different product in the same Juvéderm family, a filler used for lines and folds.

It is discussed in aesthetic circles as a 'skin booster' that can be paired with botulinum toxin or fillers. Published studies include a prospective single-arm study, a retrospective cohort and a small randomised split-face trial.
quick.mechanism: Clinicians describe injecting small amounts of gel into the dermis at several points, where the hyaluronic acid binds water and is intended to improve surface smoothness and hydration. Volite is described as a lower-concentration, longer-lasting gel than older boosters.
quick.risks: Reported effects are mainly injection-site reactions such as swelling, redness and bruising. Hyaluronic acid fillers carry rarer risks including lumps, delayed inflammatory reactions and vascular complications. It is a clinician-administered, regulated device.

lead: Juvéderm Volite is a crosslinked hyaluronic acid (HA) gel (VYC-12, also marketed as Skinvive) injected intradermally to improve skin quality attributes such as surface smoothness and hydration.[1] It is described as providing longer-lasting effects at a lower HA concentration than traditional fillers.[2]

In a prospective single-arm study, patients with moderate or severe cheek skin roughness received VYC-12 in the cheeks and other areas, and the authors reported it as safe and effective for improving facial skin topography.[1] Other published work includes a Brazilian retrospective cohort,[2] a randomised split-face trial combined with botulinum toxin,[3] and several registered manufacturer-sponsored trials.[4][5][6]
Volift is a separate Juvéderm product name; the sources reviewed contain no clinical data on it specifically.
infobox: Single-arm, retrospective and one small randomised trial

paras: Hyaluronic acid fillers are generally crosslinked to prolong their duration.[7] Volite is positioned as a skin-quality product intended to improve texture and hydration instead of volume.[1][2]

A prospective single-arm study treated subjects with moderate or severe cheek skin roughness (on the Allergan Skin Roughness Scale) with VYC-12 and reported safety and effectiveness for skin topography.[1] A retrospective cohort of patients treated between 2018 and 2019 in Rio de Janeiro examined routine-practice use and safety.[2]
A randomised, double-blind split-face trial in 25 women combined onabotulinumtoxinA with Volite (Skinvive) for periorbital wrinkles and assessed efficacy and durability.[3]

Registered trials include a healthy-volunteer study of skin quality attributes,[9] studies in China for neck lines and perioral lines,[4][5] and a phase 2/3 skin quality study.[6] Their outcomes were not available in the sources reviewed.

Hyaluronic acid fillers can cause bruising, redness, pain, swelling, lumps, and rarely vascular occlusion or granulomatous reactions.[7] A 2026 computational study modelled risk of delayed immune and fibrotic reactions across 26 fillers and genotypes; it is a modelling analysis rather than a clinical trial.[10]

timeline.event: Prospective study of VYC-12 for facial skin topography published.[1]
Retrospective cohort of Juvéderm Volite use in Brazil published.[2]
Randomised split-face trial combining botulinum toxin and Skinvive published.[3]
